title: Backlog.md: Terminal Kanban Board for Managing Tasks with AI Agents — Alex Gavrilescu, Funstage
talk_summary: Alex Gavrilescu demos Backlog.md, an MIT CLI/TUI kanban where tasks are markdown files in the repo, exposed to agents via an MCP server whose resources carry the workflow instructions and whose tools let agents search/create/update tasks. The core claim is that splitting features into small atomic tasks with explicit acceptance criteria and a written implementation plan creates three human review checkpoints and keeps each agent run inside its context window.

takeaways.technique: Three-gate task lifecycle: spec → plan → code
takeaways.what_they_do: Each task moves through explicit review checkpoints: after task creation (description + acceptance criteria), after the agent writes an implementation plan, and after code. The agent must produce a plan naming files to touch before it is allowed to implement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The first review checkpoint is after the task is created... Then you can review the implementation plan... and at the end you will review the code.

takeaways.technique: Atomic task sizing to bound context
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can define how much an AI agent should implement within a single task so that he doesn't run out of their context window

takeaways.technique: MCP resources as agent onboarding docs
takeaways.what_they_do: The MCP server exposes resources (workflow overview, task-creation guide, task-execution guide, completion/definition-of-done guide) that agents read first, plus tools for search/view/create/update. The overview resource links to the next resources so agents self-onboard.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is a special feature of MCP that backlog MD uses to instruct the agents how to use backlog MD

takeaways.technique: Acceptance criteria as testable spec + test linkage
takeaways.what_they_do: Every task has explicit, verifiable acceptance criteria, and unit tests are expected to check those criteria; completion requires checking criteria and the definition of done before moving to done.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you run unit test they should also uh check if the acceptance criteria as are met

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents are instructed to search existing tasks before creating a new one, and tasks live in git so status is visible across branches.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Before creating new task, AI agents should search if that task already exists.

takeaways.what_they_do: Independent tasks (no dependencies) are worked in parallel using git worktrees, one per task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can also work on multiple tasks in parallel using git works given that there are no dependencies.
